title: Mixed-precision KV cache compression experiments (FP8/INT8/INT4) and integration with continuous batching
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Goal: Evaluate practical KV cache compression strategies (FP8, INT8, INT4 and mixed approaches) to reduce GPU memory footprint while keeping generation quality within acceptable bounds for production inference. This ticket covers design, calibration, benchmark harness, integration with continuous batching and eviction policies, and rollout gating for the Redwood serving runtime. Target models for initial experiments: Llama2-13B and Llama2-70B; typical sequence lengths: 2048 and 8192 tokens. Key constraints: minimal per-token latency increase (<5ms median), memory savings >= 30% for full KV cache on 70B, and no more than 2% relative degradation on held-out LM metrics for acceptable tiers.
acceptance_criteria: Quantization pipeline implemented in runtime prototype (FP8/INT8/INT4 + per-channel scaling) and can be toggled per-model
Benchmark results for 13B and 70B across seq lens 2048/8192 showing memory savings, throughput, and quality metrics (PPL, token-level exact-match on eval prompts, embedding cosine drift)
Integration plan for continuous batching to avoid full-cache dequant for each request (batch-aware dequant strategy documented and implemented in prototype)
Fallback policy defined: automatic reversion to FP16 when regression triggers exceed thresholds in Canary runs
Design doc + rollout checklist and a PR with unit and integration tests
experiment_plan: Calibration: collect per-layer/key statistics on representative workloads (prefix distributions, value ranges) to compute per-channel scales using 99.9th percentile and MSE minimization options
Formats: implement FP8 (E4M3-like) pathway, symmetric INT8 and two INT4 strategies (per-channel and 2-bit packing with bias correction)
Storage layouts: try contiguous compressed layout vs. split hot/cold cache (hot keys kept in FP16, cold keys compressed)
Runtime: microbench CUDA kernels for on-the-fly dequant versus batched dequant for selected keys only; measure latency/throughput trade-offs

Evaluation: run LM perplexity, token accuracy on Redwood eval suite (prompts with long-range dependencies), embedding drift (cosine) for retrieval-heavy workloads, and generation quality human spot-checks
A/B plan: small Canary on Dedicated pool with 10% traffic and regression alerting tied to prompt-based eval sets
observations: FP8 path yields best quality-density trade-off on 13B: median PPL delta <0.6% compared to FP16 while saving ~36% memory for full KV cache
INT8 gives decent memory savings (~45%) but exhibits 1.2-2.5% PPL regressions on 70B at long context (8192), likely due to per-layer activation distribution tails
Aggressive INT4 causes large degradations for tasks with arithmetic and factual recall beyond 1024 tokens; unsuitable as default for long-context models
Mixed strategy (recent keys FP16 + older keys INT8) reduces perceptible regressions while achieving ~40% memory reduction and fewer cache evictions during high-concurrency workloads
Dequant overhead: naive per-request dequant adds ~3-6ms median latency on Ampere A10G; batched dequant amortized across continuous batching reduces this to ~0.5-1.5ms per request
Batch-aware dequant (only dequant keys referenced by active batch) cuts memory bandwidth and reduces stalls during KV lookup, improving tokens/sec on high-concurrency scenarios by 6-12%
On older Ampere/Turing hardware without FP8 support, FP8 path falls back to emulation which increases latency; need opt-out by hardware capability detection
decisions: Do a staged approach: enable FP8 as the preferred compressed format for mid-sized models (<=13B) for runtime-1.20, enable INT8 mixed strategy as opt-in for large models with Canary gating
Do NOT enable INT4 globally for long-context models; keep INT4 as an experimental, per-customer opt-in with explicit QA
Implement hot/cold split in KV cache: keep last N tokens (configurable, default 512) in FP16 and compress older entries to INT8/FP8 to balance recall and memory
Add hardware capability probe at startup and prefer native FP8 kernels when available; otherwise fall back to INT8 emulation or skip compression
Expose per-model compression policy in model manifest and Console (compression: off | fp8 | int8-hotcold | int4-experimental)
Integrate dequantation with continuous batching so that dequant work is scheduled as part of batch assembly to amortize overhead
next_steps: Finalize CUDA kernels for batched dequant and publish microbench results in runtime PR
Automate calibration step in model onboarding pipeline with stored calibration tables in model artifact
Create Canary run on dedicated cluster (runtime-1.20-canary) with rolling monitors on PPL, token-latency, and embedding drift; duration 72h
Add detailed observability: token-level quality traces, per-request cache-compression hits, and dequant time in Console dashboards
Write runbook for rollback and alert thresholds for Canary (PPL +1.5% or embedding cosine < 0.95 on retrieval prompts triggers rollback)
Plan a small user-facing experiment with a friendly customer on Dedicated to validate empirical UX impact
